column2: every row the registered WinitWindowDelegate and WinitView hold agrees with the runtime's own authority, and each class claims the protocols its rows come from

a composition ran through the ported WinitView's NSTextInputClient rows — preedit, cursor conversion, commit and the candidate-window rectangle — and with Option as Alt, no U.S. Option dead key (E, U, I, N, `) started a composition where the same key without it did, and Option+B arrived as b, not ∫

the real tab strip answered every question — every state its drawing matrix names, and all four declared classes read off live objects against the runtime's own authority — and the menu bar's real status item held This Mac as its glance counts it, and listed a box that stopped its agent above an older report whose row's tip says its program carries on meanwhile, and a landing's Done for you row and worker row whose tips say what aterm checked, and at each fleet access level showed that level's lock beside the caret with the level checked in its Fleet Access submenu, no menu of the item's own and no lock out of a fleet

the real window answered every question — title, style mask, geometry, limits, theme, drag-and-drop, close and fullscreen — callbacks, redraws and native termination raised inside real NSAlert modal loops waited for their outer handlers; the production Rename This Mac alert's actual field-editor focus callback waited for its user_event handler, Cancel emitted no rename request, and Destroyed preceded LoopExiting; a panic from a deferred redraw returned through the pump rather than aborting at the Objective-C block boundary; and the exit, in the turn a click answered another real NSAlert, closed only winit's own windows and none of the alert's

every NSEvent-taking WinitView row and sendEvent: survived a real NSEvent of every type AppKit can deliver, and flagsChanged: retained its Relayed classifier verdict through deferred KeyboardInput and ModifiersChanged delivery; the exception control was contained and the panic control aborted

a real window's display link ran the deck's clock: by the link's own timestamps its ticks each named a period the screen runs, targeted the coming vsync (the median tick's and the best tick's lead both positive) and never stalled LINK_SILENCE, and the clock's hang detector never tripped; paused, the CADisplayLink said so (-isPaused) and fired nothing while the clock's detector tripped on real time and timed the window as one with no link, and the restarted link's first tick resumed the clock; the link ticked while the main run loop ran in NSEventTrackingRunLoopMode; and closing the window invalidated every link its view made (a weak reference to each CADisplayLink, which its run loop retains until -invalidate, loaded nil after the close, and no tick fired for a vsync after it)

the Stop Worker sheet came up on a real NSAlert with its title, body and buttons; a click on Stop answered yes, and a click on Cancel, Return and Escape each no; and Rename This Mac's real alert showed its two fields, its buttons and the live line for what was typed into them through their field editor, disabled Rename for a number the read it was handed through the main queue gave another Mac (Return then did nothing and Escape cancelled), redrew the line when a read landed after typing, moved each untouched field to a read newer than the window's view while a field typed into before it kept its words and the caret stayed in the field being edited, emptied the Number field of a number a migration still waits on until it was typed to claim it, and answered Rename with only what was typed
